what_it_does: This paper tackles a fundamental problem in tiny implantable medical devices like pacemakers and neural sensors: they need wireless power sent to them (so no battery wears out) AND a way to send data back wirelessly. Usually, increasing power transfer kills data rate, or vice versa. The solution uses a technique called frequency-splitting enhancement (FSE): split the wireless signal into two different frequencies—one carries power, the other carries data—and then adjust the receiver's electronics in real-time to accept less power when data is being sent. The result is a system that works through a receiver coil smaller than a grain of rice while delivering 60% end-to-end efficiency and high-speed data (1 megabit/second).
